title: Is the agent healthy?
objective: Learners watch one day of an AI agent's latency and error rate, see a prompt or model change drift both upward, and learn why a control chart with limits and a view of the whole latency distribution (p50 against p95) catch the drift hours before a dashboard of averages does.

recommended.why: A control chart is a standard line chart with three extra lines; Chart.js draws it from configuration and the breach points stand out as red dots.

alternative.why: The control chart shows when the median crossed a line; violins and boxes show how the whole distribution changed shape. Which one would convince an on-call engineer, and which one a product owner?

assumptions: Traffic, latencies and error rates are seeded synthetic numbers for a fictional agent; the shapes are realistic, the values are not a benchmark
Latency is log-normal around a baseline that rises with load above about 1,200 requests an hour (queueing); 40 samples per half-hour bucket
The change at the chosen hour drifts the median up by about 55 % and the error rate from 1 % to 6 % over about two hours
Control limits come from the first six hours of the day (mean ± k σ of the half-hour medians); the change is never earlier than 08:00, so the baseline is clean
A breach is the first half-hour whose median falls outside the limits; error rate has its own upper limit
Playback runs one hour per second
units: error rate: share of requests that fail
time: hour of the day, half-hour buckets
checkDescription: The limits equal mean ± k σ of the first twelve half-hour medians, the first breach is the first bucket after the baseline outside them, every flagged bucket is really outside, the baseline is entirely before the change, and both latency and error rate are higher after the change than before.
expectAtDefaults: m.firstAfter !== null && m.detectDelay > 0 && m.falseAlarms === 0 && m.shift.afterP50 > m.shift.beforeP50

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the alert threshold to 2 σ before you play. Will the breach come earlier, and what else might happen before the change ships?
learnerPrompts.explain: Raise the traffic to 2,000 requests an hour. The baseline latency is higher but the drift is still caught. Why do the limits still work, and what would break them?
